bill.title: To reauthorize the Young Women’s Breast Health Education and Awareness Requires Learning Young Act of 2009.
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.

industries.rationale: The bill funds screening, diagnostic, and treatment services that hospitals and health systems deliver to low-income patients.
The bill supports diagnostic testing and treatment services for breast and cervical cancer, which involve medical devices and pharmaceuticals.
The program targets uninsured individuals, potentially affecting the pool of patients who might otherwise seek coverage or remain uninsured.

bill.plainSummary: This bill extends federal funding through 2030–2031 for Centers for Disease Control and Prevention programs that help low-income and uninsured women access breast and cervical cancer screening and treatment. It gives states more flexibility in how they spend grant money and requires a government report on how many people are served and what barriers prevent access. The bill also continues education campaigns and research focused on breast cancer in younger women.

plain.whoItTouches: People with cancer, and the people caring for them.

bill.title: Veterans SPORT Act
bill.latestActionText: Forwarded by Subcommittee to Full Committee by Voice Vote.

industries.rationale: Medical device manufacturers that produce adaptive prosthetics and terminal devices would see expanded demand through VA procurement.
VA health systems would need to furnish and fit these specialized prosthetic devices as part of their medical services.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would require the Department of Veterans Affairs to provide adaptive prosthetic limbs and terminal devices designed for sports and recreational activities to eligible veterans. Currently, VA medical services cover standard prosthetics; this legislation would expand that definition to include specialized equipment for athletic and outdoor activities. The change would make these recreational prostheses available as part of standard VA medical care rather than requiring separate approval or funding.

bill.title: SOAR Act of 2025
bill.latestActionText: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.

industries.rationale: Medical equipment suppliers providing oxygen equipment and related supplies would face new payment methods and regulatory requirements.
Respiratory therapists and providers prescribing oxygen would see new coverage and payment structures under Medicare.
Medicare payment changes for oxygen services could affect supplemental insurance coverage and coordination of benefits.

bill.plainSummary: This bill changes how Medicare pays for supplemental oxygen equipment and services. Instead of using a competitive bidding system, it would establish separate payments that adjust for inflation. It would also formally cover services provided by respiratory therapists, require a standardized electronic prescription form, and give patients specific rights such as choosing their own oxygen supplier.

plain.whoItTouches: Anyone who sees a doctor or pays for care.

bill.title: HALT Fentanyl Act
bill.latestActionText: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

industries.rationale: The bill changes registration and licensing requirements for pharmaceutical researchers working with controlled substances and affects the regulatory classification of fentanyl-related compounds.
The bill establishes new criminal penalties and quantity thresholds that will affect defense attorneys and prosecutors handling drug trafficking cases.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would permanently classify all fentanyl-related substances as Schedule I controlled substances, meaning they would be treated as having high abuse potential and no accepted medical use. It sets the same criminal penalties and quantity thresholds for fentanyl-related substances as currently apply to fentanyl analogues. The bill also creates a streamlined registration process for researchers studying Schedule I substances and makes it easier for registered researchers to conduct certain activities without additional permits.

plain.whoItTouches: People caught up in the criminal law, and victims of crime.

bill.title: Providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Environmental Protection Agency relating to "Waste Emissions Charge for Petroleum and Natural Gas Systems: Procedures for Facilitating Compliance, Including Netting and Exemptions".

industries.rationale: The resolution directly eliminates a waste emissions charge on oil and gas facilities that exceed methane emission thresholds.

bill.plainSummary: This resolution would eliminate a rule that charges oil and gas facilities an annual fee when they exceed certain limits for methane and greenhouse gas emissions. The Environmental Protection Agency published the rule in November 2024 as part of a program to reduce methane waste from petroleum and natural gas operations. If passed, the resolution would nullify this fee structure and the compliance procedures associated with it.

plain.whoItTouches: Anyone who buys fuel or heats a home. People living near a road, a plant or a port.

bill.title: PRECISE Act
bill.latestActionText: Referred to the Subcommittee on Conservation, Research, and Biotechnology.

industries.rationale: The bill directly expands USDA loan and conservation programs to fund precision agriculture equipment and practices for crop and livestock producers.
The bill creates new federal support for precision agriculture technology and equipment, expanding the market for sensors, software, and data systems used in farming.
The bill would increase demand for precision agriculture equipment such as GPS-guided machinery, variable-rate applicators, and monitoring devices.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would expand several USDA programs to support precision agriculture—technologies and practices that help farmers use seeds, fertilizer, water, and other inputs more efficiently. It would allow conservation loans, environmental quality incentives, and stewardship programs to fund precision agriculture equipment and practices. The bill would also direct USDA to use third-party providers for technical assistance on soil health and nutrient management.

plain.whoItTouches: Farmers, and anyone who buys food.

bill.title: Billion Dollar Boondoggle Act
bill.latestActionText: Received in the Senate. Read twice. Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 467.

industries.rationale: Defense contractors frequently work on large federal projects that may trigger the reporting thresholds for schedule delays or cost overruns.
Construction and engineering firms execute major federal infrastructure and building projects that could exceed cost estimates or timelines.
Technology contractors working on large federal IT modernization and systems projects may face increased reporting obligations if projects run over budget or schedule.

bill.plainSummary: This bill requires the Office of Management and Budget to collect and publish an annual report on federal projects that are either more than five years behind schedule or have gone at least $1 billion over their original cost estimate. Agencies must explain the reasons for delays and cost overruns, describe changes to project scope, and disclose any bonuses or incentive fees paid. The report must be submitted to Congress and posted online.

plain.whoItTouches: Anyone who deals with a federal agency.
